---
title: "Quiz: Mean, variance, and SD"
---

[Exercises](12-variation.qmd) · [Lecture slides](../lectures/12-variation/lec.qmd)

Try each question before opening its hint or answer.

---

**Q1.** For growth values 12, 14, and 16 mm, calculate the mean, sample variance,
and sample SD, with units.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
The squared deviations from 14 are 4, 0, and 4. Sample variance divides
their sum by $n-1$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Mean **14 mm**; sample variance $(4+0+4)/2 = 4$ **mm²**;
sample SD $\sqrt{4}=2$ **mm**.
:::

---

**Q2.** What will this return, and why?

```r
mean(c(10, 10, 10, 100))
median(c(10, 10, 10, 100))
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
The mean uses every value; the median uses the ordered middle values.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The mean is **32.5** and median **10**. The large value strongly affects
the mean; neither result is an arithmetic error.
:::

---

**Q3.** A vector has mean 14 mm and SD 2 mm. What happens when 10 mm is added to
every value? What happens when the original values are divided by ten to
express centimetres?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
A common addition leaves deviations unchanged. Unit conversion rescales
both measurements and their deviations.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Adding 10 mm gives mean **24 mm**, SD **2 mm**. Converting the original
values gives mean **1.4 cm**, SD **0.2 cm** and variance **0.04 cm²**.
:::

---

**Q4.** Two groups have the same mean but SDs of 1 and 6 mm. Which statement is
supported?

(i) The second group has greater observed spread.  

(ii) Every second-group plant is larger.  

(iii) The second group was measured incorrectly.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
SD describes variation among observations, not its cause.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
(i). The observations in the second group vary more around their mean.
SD alone does not identify biological or measurement causes.
:::

---

**Q5.** A synthesis run collects 0.62 g from a supplied maximum of 1.00 g.
Percentage yield is `100 * collected / maximum`. What is the yield? If
another run yields 70%, how many percentage points higher is that?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Use the supplied ratio, then subtract the percentages.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
**62%** yield; 70% is **8 percentage points** higher. The difference is
not an 8% relative increase.
:::
